doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

chapter: New York studio and sideman work
title: Working with Ben Webster
summary: Playing with Webster was inspirational with Mel Lewis and Richard Davis, but his volatile temper, including an incident with police at the Half Note, was scary.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: I’m looking at some of the guys you played with — Ben Webster, what was he like to work with?

Well he was pretty scary. I mean he was inspirational to me. I was in the middle of my Duke Ellington period when I got the job so I was really ready for it you know. And it was a wonderful learning experience for me and so much fun musically, I can’t tell you. It was a really nourishing musical thing. And we had great rhythm players — Mel Lewis was the drummer and Richard Davis was the bass player. I never had so much fun being in a rhythm section. They were so good. And they just, we just sailed along. It was wonderful. But when I say it was scary, Ben was — we never knew what to expect from Ben. He would explode, his temper would flare unexpectedly and it was scary sometimes, at the Half Note one time he mouthed off to a policeman and the rest of the evening was really upsetting. I mean they backed him up against a wall and they called squad cars and it was just a nightmare. He had this volatile temper.
